identityReview: Matched Atlassian cofounder Scott Farquhar across corporate leadership, UNSW alumni history, TCA leadership releases, Pledge 1% and Skip Capital. Wikipedia supports Australian nationality and 1979 birth year; month/day and private family details omitted.
lifeStatusEvidence: TCA February 17, 2026 release reports his remarks as chair at that day’s AGM and renewal as director. Current corporate and TCA leadership pages support ongoing roles.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Opened primary TCA releases, Pledge 1% appointment and history, Skip Capital team and Wikipedia; reused Atlassian leadership, transition, IPO-day and anniversary posts and UNSW alumni history actually read in preceding cofounder review.
sourceReview.scope: Identity, current and historical leadership, education, cofounding, philanthropy framework and dated milestones.
corrections: UNSW records Farquhar BSc 2003 and Cannon-Brookes BSc 2002; both received 2013 alumni awards. Do not infer the same graduation year or a postgraduate degree.

Atlassian retrospective explicitly places cofounding in 2002. Loose reference to 23 years in 2024 transition letter is not a basis for back-calculating founding year. Shared founder and team contributions retained.

August 31, 2024 is the last co-CEO day in his own transition statement, not its April announcement date. Remained board member and special adviser. Current CEO is Cannon-Brookes; Farquhar is not Atlassian chair or current CEO.

TCA March 12, 2025 announcement explicitly schedules transition from Robyn Denholm for late March. Timeline dates announcement and preserves effective-period distinction. February 17, 2026 release renews a three-year DIRECTOR term, not an explicitly fixed chair term.
Pledge 1% appointment is dated May 7, 2025 on the primary release, not a later repost date. The release calls him incoming board chair.

Pledge 1% history places initial Atlassian/Salesforce invitation on Giving Tuesday 2014 with a target for Giving Tuesday 2015. The 2025 appointment release loosely says started in 2015. Timeline explicitly describes the 2014 initiative, not legal incorporation, and preserves discrepancy here.

Pledge 1% flexible framework permits one or more of equity, profit, product and employee time; not mandatory donation of all four. Commitments are not proof of delivered gifts. No aggregate donated sum asserted.
Skip Capital website identifies Kim Jackson as cofounder, CEO and CIO and Farquhar as cofounder. No CEO role assigned to him and no uncorroborated exact founding date retained.
December 10, 2015 company post confirms Nasdaq trading had begun under TEAM and both founders rang the bell; not merely a planned IPO.

Historical co-CEO labels on Pledge 1% narrative and portrait metadata do not override current corporate leadership. No current wealth estimate, stock-sale proceeds or quantified philanthropic impact asserted.
